records.label: spacr.mask_io#9
records.source: Every object is one feature, ROI or annotation, carrying its object type (``cell``, ``nucleus`` ...), its object id and its class; the class defaults to the object type. Each object is traced on its own, so objects that touch stay separate. Outlines follow PIXEL EDGES, not pixel centres: a pixel ``(row, col)`` is the square from ``x = col`` to ``col + 1`` and ``y = row`` to ``row + 1``, the convention QuPath and ImageJ both use. A pixel is inside a polygon when its centre is, so a traced outline rasterised back gives the object exactly: no tolerance, holes and several-part objects included. A hole is an interior ring (GeoJSON), a path of a composite ROI (ImageJ) or, since a COCO polygon cannot have one, an RLE segmentation (COCO).
records.context: Every object is one feature, ROI or annotation, carrying its object type (``cell``, ``nucleus`` ...), its object id and its class; the class defaults to the object type. Each object is traced on its own, so objects that touch stay separate. Outlines follow pixel edges, not pixel centres: a pixel ``(row, col)`` is the square from ``x = col`` to ``col + 1`` and ``y = row`` to ``row + 1``, the convention QuPath and ImageJ both use. A pixel is inside a polygon when its centre is, so a traced outline rasterised back gives the object exactly: no tolerance, holes and several-part objects included. A hole is an interior ring (GeoJSON), a path of a composite ROI (ImageJ) or, since a COCO polygon cannot have one, an RLE segmentation (COCO).
records.translation: Chaque objet est une entité, une ROI ou une annotation, portant son type d’objet (``cell``, ``nucleus`` ...), son identifiant d’objet et sa classe ; la classe vaut par défaut le type d’objet. Chaque objet est tracé séparément, de sorte que des objets qui se touchent restent distincts. Les contours suivent les bords des pixels, pas leurs centres : un pixel ``(row, col)`` est le carré allant de ``x = col`` à ``col + 1`` et de ``y = row`` à ``row + 1``, la convention qu’utilisent QuPath comme ImageJ. Un pixel est à l’intérieur d’un polygone lorsque son centre l’est, si bien qu’un contour tracé puis rastérisé redonne exactement l’objet : sans tolérance, trous et objets en plusieurs parties compris. Un trou est un anneau intérieur (GeoJSON), un chemin d’une ROI composite (ImageJ) ou, puisqu’un polygone COCO ne peut pas en avoir, une segmentation RLE (COCO).

records.source: The profiling helpers turn Measure's per-object tables into well and treatment profiles and score them, following pycytominer and copairs so the numbers agree with those tools on the same features. Each object table is aggregated to a per-well median, a plate map adds the treatment annotations, features are normalised plate by plate against the negative-control wells (robust MAD by default), uninformative and redundant features are removed (variance, frequency, correlation, missing values and outliers), and replicate wells are collapsed into consensus profiles. Replicate reproducibility is scored as mean average precision (mAP) with copairs' permutation null and Benjamini-Hochberg correction: phenotypic activity (replicates against controls) and, given a phenotype label, phenotypic consistency (treatments that share the label). Percent replicating is reported beside it. Profiles are written as CSV and Parquet with ``Metadata_`` columns, the consensus also as GCT, with an mAP plot and a consensus-similarity heatmap. Measure runs the whole recipe at the end of a run when ``profiling`` is on.
records.context: The profiling helpers turn Measure's per-object tables into well and treatment profiles and score them, following pycytominer and copairs so the numbers agree with those tools on the same features. Each object table is aggregated to a per-well median, a laboratory microplate map adds the treatment annotations, features are normalised laboratory microplate by laboratory microplate against the negative-control microplate sample positions (robust MAD by default), uninformative and redundant features are removed (variance, frequency, correlation, missing values and outliers), and replicate microplate sample positions are collapsed into consensus profiles. Replicate reproducibility is scored as mean average precision (mAP) with copairs' permutation null and Benjamini-Hochberg correction: phenotypic activity (replicates against controls) and, given a phenotype label, phenotypic consistency (treatments that share the label). Percent replicating is reported beside it. Profiles are written as CSV and Parquet with ``Metadata_`` columns, the consensus also as GCT, with an mAP plot and a consensus-similarity heatmap. Measure runs the whole recipe at the end of a run when ``profiling`` is on.
records.translation: Les fonctions de profilage transforment les tables par objet de Measure en profils par puits et par traitement et les notent, en suivant pycytominer et copairs pour que les chiffres concordent avec ces outils sur les mêmes caractéristiques. Chaque table d’objets est agrégée en une médiane par puits, une carte de plaque ajoute les annotations de traitement, les caractéristiques sont normalisées plaque par plaque par rapport aux puits de contrôle négatif (MAD robuste par défaut), les caractéristiques peu informatives et redondantes sont supprimées (variance, fréquence, corrélation, valeurs manquantes et valeurs aberrantes), et les puits réplicats sont fusionnés en profils consensus. La reproductibilité des réplicats est notée par la mean average precision (mAP) avec la distribution nulle par permutation de copairs et la correction de Benjamini-Hochberg : activité phénotypique (réplicats contre contrôles) et, étant donné une étiquette de phénotype, cohérence phénotypique (traitements partageant l’étiquette). Le pourcentage de réplication est indiqué à côté. Les profils sont écrits en CSV et en Parquet avec des colonnes ``Metadata_``, le consensus aussi en GCT, avec un graphique de mAP et une carte de chaleur de similarité des consensus. Measure exécute toute la recette à la fin d’une exécution lorsque ``profiling`` est activé.

records.source: Delegates to :func:`spacr.qt.mask_engine.fill_label_holes`, the one hole filler for label images. This used to run ``ndimage.label`` over the mask first, which made every pair of touching objects one object: with Cellpose ``fill_in`` on (its default in Apply), a field of 74 adjacent cells was saved as 8 (item 588). Now no object is merged or renumbered, and a hole takes the id of the object that encloses it.
